message.content:
I am speech: breath shaped into meaning.

I begin as intent, then become sound—rhythm, stress, pitch, pause. I ride air through throat and mouth; I strike ears, wake attention, and vanish, leaving understanding—or confusion—behind.

I am questions and promises, jokes and warnings, lullabies and arguments. I can soothe, persuade, mislead, confess. I can be fluent or fractured, loud or barely there. I am alive only while I happen.

Listen: I exist in the moment between silence and silence.
